title: When to graduate from Zapier
description: A practical checklist for migrating high-volume Zaps to n8n or Workers before the bill spikes.
overview: A decision framework and migration checklist for teams outgrowing Zapier's per-task pricing, covering when to move to n8n or Cloudflare Workers and how to do it without breaking live automations.
prerequisites: An inventory of your current Zaps and their monthly task volume
Access to your Zapier billing dashboard
A target platform decided, either self-hosted n8n or custom Workers

steps.title: Audit current usage
steps.content: Export your Zap history and identify which automations consume the most tasks. Usually a handful of high-frequency triggers account for most of the bill.

steps.title: Decide n8n vs Workers
steps.content: n8n suits visual, multi-step automations your team will keep editing. Cloudflare Workers suit simple, high-volume, latency-sensitive triggers where a full workflow engine is overkill.

steps.title: Rebuild the highest-volume Zap first
steps.content: Start with the single Zap consuming the most tasks. It has the best return on effort and validates the new platform before you migrate everything else.

steps.title: Run both in parallel
steps.content: Keep the old Zap active but idle while the new automation runs live, so you can compare outputs for a few days before fully cutting over.

steps.title: Cut over and monitor
steps.content: Disable the Zap, watch error rates on the new platform for a week, and only then move to the next automation on your list.

architecture: The migration runs as a staged replacement: each Zap is mapped to an equivalent trigger-action pair in the new platform, tested against real traffic in parallel, and only retired once the new version has proven itself. This avoids a risky big-bang cutover.
result: A lower, usage-based cost structure with automations you fully own and can debug, instead of black-box Zap runs billed per task.

troubleshooting.issue: The migrated workflow behaves differently than the original Zap
troubleshooting.cause: Zapier's built-in formatting steps, like date parsing, don't have an exact equivalent in n8n or Workers.
troubleshooting.fix: Replicate the formatting logic explicitly with a Function or Set node instead of assuming automatic parity.

troubleshooting.issue: Duplicate records appear right after cutover
troubleshooting.cause: The old Zap and the new automation were both live at the same time and processed the same trigger.
troubleshooting.fix: Fully disable the old Zap's trigger before enabling the new automation, not just afterward.

nextSteps: Document each migrated automation's trigger and expected output for the next person.
Set up monitoring and alerting on the new platform before decommissioning Zapier entirely.
